ELO 'high provisional rating' is NOT implemented generically. ratings.go uses a single flat DefaultInitialRating=1500.0 for EVERY unseen benchmark regardless of tier (verified: ratings.go:16,48-53). There is no tier-biased provisional rating; frontier benchmarks enter at 1500 like all others and converge via pass/fail. Scope item 3 ('verify + a test is enough') is satisfiable, but the doc's phrasing 'enter with a HIGH provisional ELO' is aspirational, not literal. Plan treats item 3 as: verify unseen benchmarks are handled generically (they are) + add a regression test asserting a never-before-seen bench id enters at DefaultInitialRating and updates on pass/fail. Do NOT invent tier-biased seeding (out of scope, no data to calibrate).

CURATION.md has NO '4-dimension >=95% demote rule'. The '>=95% on ALL FOUR std/agent x AILANG/Python dimensions' phrasing exists ONLY in the design doc, not in benchmarks/CURATION.md. CURATION.md §5 Demotion actually says: core->stretch requires '<30% AILANG pass for two baselines AND the benchmark is accurate'. §4 IsSaturated flags '100% across every model x language'. So the doc's demote rule and CURATION.md's demote rule DISAGREE. Resolution in this sprint: (a) apply the CONSERVATIVE reading — a benchmark is a demotion candidate only if saturated (100%/near-100%) on ALL FOUR dimensions with data present; (b) codify this 4-dimension rule INTO CURATION.md §5 as an explicit new 'saturation demotion' row (the doc mandates using it, so make CURATION.md the real source of truth); (c) document every per-benchmark decision. Never demote on a dimension that has no data (matches doc's 'do not demote on incomplete evidence').

Agent-mode data is NOT sparse for the demotion audit. The task framing ('agent-mode data is sparse') refers to the TOP-LEVEL eval_results/agent/ dir (motoko/ollama scratch). But the BANKED baseline eval_results/baselines/v0.25.0/agent/ has 444 files = 6 models (claude-sonnet-4-6, gpt5-4-mini, opencode-or-{deepseek-v4-flash, deepseek-v4-pro, glm-5-1, minimax-m3}) x both langs, covering all 15 demotion-list benchmarks (12 files each, ailang+python). The 4-dimension audit IS feasible from banked data. Caveat: agent uses a DIFFERENT, smaller model set (6, incl. local/opencode) than standard (11 cloud). Record that a 100%-agent verdict rests on 6 models, not 11 — weaker evidence, but present. (verified: ls counts + per-benchmark grep)
